title: Hodges's soprano as a second horn
summary: Waters confirms that the Boston gigs with Hodges were soprano only, and that Hodges's main horn was alto, with soprano his practice instrument.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Right. Benny, one last little question before this tape reel runs out. When we were talkin' about Johnny Hodges in Boston and you and him giggin', you playing piano, him playing soprano, him playing piano and you playing soprano - did he play only soprano then or did he also play alto?
No, we had it only the soprano, see. That was on account of us not havin' too much in ours hands, you know, we wasn't - and then Johnny wanted to get the practice on the soprano and so did I -
But did he play alto at that time?
No, not in that, in those sessions.
Not in - but I mean in general, did he play alto -
Oh, that was his role, on alto.
So soprano was his second horn.
Yeah, sure, he just started on the soprano. Alto. (mike noise, end of reel 3. End of interview.)
